messages:
mia: FYI, deploy went out ~10m ago and we're seeing a host-side tail bump on streaming paths. p95 from ~70ms -> ~120ms for small chunked requests. CPU in 'parse' region spikes. :eyes:

raj: can you paste the flame/pprof? curious if kernel selection or batching changes landed.

mia: quick collect i ran locally — attaching snippets: 
```
# quick pprof collect
PPROF=/tmp/pprof.cpu
python -m pyinstrument --include-files runtime/ingress/*.py --output /tmp/pyi.html
curl -sS http://localhost:6060/debug/pprof/profile?seconds=30 > $PPROF
pprof -top -nodefraction=0.01 /tmp/pprof.cpu
```

mia: top output (trimmed):
```
30.2%  parse_frame
18.5%  http2_read
12.1%  tokenization.tokenize
8.2%   kvcache.lookup
6.0%   socket.readv
```

olivia: interesting that read/parse are both high. any change in chunking logic in gateway last deploy?

mia: yes, we landed the streaming-frag optimization that tries to flush micro-chunks earlier to reduce latency for long streams. appears to increase number of small frames for short requests.

sam: that matches earlier bench notes — more syscalls and more parse invocations. For short requests, overhead dominates.

raj: two hypotheses: 1) increased syscall / small write overhead (socket/readv/writev) 2) more KV cache churn because tokenization produces different prefix shapes -> new cache keys.

noa: can we confirm cache miss rate? metrics for kvcache.miss/req?

mia: kv miss rate jumped from 6% -> 18% for the sampled endpoints in last hour.

perf-bot: Automated flamegraph: https://perf.redwood/internal/fg/4698765432 (generated) :robot_face:

olivia: proposal: reintroduce a tiny coalescing window for host ingress: if a connection sends lots of tiny writes within 3-5ms, coalesce into a single parse pass. keep it off for long-lived streaming where we already flush incrementally.

sam: careful: adding delay may hurt interactive streams. we should make it adaptive: rate-based + max-delay cap. e.g., coalesce if writes/sec > X and oldest-chunk-age < 5ms and total-buffer < 2KB.

raj: also check kernel selection fallback: the runtime picks a quantized kernel for short sequences, maybe the new fragmentation changes seq-length histogram and we fall back to slow kernel more often. can we dump kernel selection counts?

mia: dumped counters: 
```
kernel_choice.short_fast: 62%
kernel_choice.generic: 38%  # up from 25% pre-deploy
```

mia: so yes, more generic kernels taken. likely because fragmented frames present as many tiny sequences.

olivia: additional mitigations: (1) coalesce small frames pre-tokenize, (2) bias kernel selector with a small hysteresis so transient tiny sequences don't flip kernel, (3) make KV cache key normalize by trimming trailing partial tokens for in-flight frames.

noa: I can prototype pre-tokenize coalescer. quick perf test plan: A/B deploy with coalescer on a small % of hosts and run the streaming microbench (100k short requests) and measure p95 and kv miss.

sam: +1. also add a histogram on "chunks_per_request" and "avg_chunk_size" to surface regressions earlier.

raj: one more: check HTTP/2 header fragmentation — our header-parsing code allocates per-header when fragments cross frames. if we coalesce at socket layer we should reduce allocations.

mia: reproduced allocation stack for header parse: 
```
runtime/ingress/http2_parse.go: allocateHeaderField
runtime/ingress/parse.go: parseHeaders
runtime/proto/unpack.go: newSlice
```

perf-bot: Regression alert created: reg-4698765432, linked to dashboard /dash/regressions/4698765432 :bell:

olivia: OK next steps:
- noa: prototype coalescer (w/ 3ms default, adaptive) -> PR to infra-ingress
- mia: add kernel-selection telemetry + histograms for chunk metrics
- raj: add KV-key normalization experiment and check hit rate
- sam: run A/B microbench and call out tail latencies

mia: I'll create the A/B on canary group and attach bench script. thanks all. :thumbsup:

noa: volunteering now, will push a quick prototype by EOD and attach perf numbers tomorrow.

raj: leaving a note to consider whether we should expose a deploy-time flag for coalescing to ops for quick rollback if interaction apps complain.

sam: noted. I'll add a metric + alert if p95 regresses >10% post-rollout.

mia: closing loop — will post results here once microbench runs finish.
